newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgacom to cut thousands of jobs - television.
newsitem.headline: Belgacom to cut thousands of jobs - television.

text.p: Belgium's partly-privatised telephone company Belgacom will cut thousands of jobs next year as part of a drastic restructuring programme to groom it for the liberalised European telecommunications market, Belgian BRTN television said on Monday.
It said that even the most optimistic sources forecast the loss of "a few thousands of jobs" from a workforce of 26,000.
Thousands of others will have to change jobs within the company, which will invest heavily training, it said. There would however be no layoffs, it said.
Belgacom was not immediately available for comment.
Belgacom's workforce had been guaranteed job security until 1997 by management.
The company is owned 49.9 percent by a consortium including Ameritech, Tele Danmark and Singapore Telecom. The remaining shares are held by the Belgian state.
